records.text: The Network Contagion Research Institute produced a report featuring Owens's face that claimed 'Christ is King' had become antisemitic, in partnership with Johnnie Moore and Jordan Peterson.

appearances.snippet: They were also the ones that came up with a report with my face on it claiming that Christ is King was suddenly anti-Semitic. ... And Dr. Jordan Peterson all trying to convince you in a psyop that if you think Christ is king, you might be falling for the dark tetrad.

verification.notes: The NCRI report exists, includes Jordan Peterson and Johnnie Moore among its authors, and discusses Candace Owens while arguing extremists weaponized the phrase Christ is King. sources.title: Thy Name in Vain: How Online Extremists Hijacked Christ is King
sources.relevance: The NCRI report itself establishes its authors, treatment of Owens, and narrower claim that extremists weaponized the phrase.

records.text: Owens said NCRI had previously promoted the claim that 'Christ is King' was antisemitic and released that report during Lent.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: They do focused reports on, I think, really just me, things that I say. And they were really pushing and pedaling a couple years ago that Christ is King is anti-Semitic. They released this report during Lent. It backfired, obviously.

verification.notes: Transcript context reviewed. The March 13, 2025 NCRI report documented extremist and antisemitic actors weaponizing the phrase 'Christ is King'; it did not classify the Christian profession itself as inherently antisemitic. The report was released during Lent, which began March 5, 2025. The statement is therefore accurate about timing and the controversy but overstates the report's conclusion.

sources.title: Thy Name in Vain: How Online Extremists Hijacked 'Christ is King'
sources.relevance: Primary NCRI report; documents extremist weaponization of the phrase and distinguishes that conduct from the phrase's ordinary Christian meaning.
